steps.title: fetchData pulls a level-sized batch
steps.why: It asks the Dragon Ball API for as many characters as the level needs and ignores replies for a level no longer picked.

steps.title: A failed fetch is only logged
steps.why: Errors are caught and logged, never thrown, so a failed request leaves an empty board instead of a crash.

steps.title: A new level means a new fetch
steps.why: This effect clears the old cards and fetches again whenever the level changes, marking the old request stale.

steps.title: Picking a level on the title screen
steps.why: A level button stores the choice in MainSection, and stops the click from also pressing Fight.

steps.title: Fight switches to the game
steps.why: Fight plays its sound, flips MainSection to the play page and turns the music on.

recap.title: The level sets the board size
recap.body: levelSettings gives how many cards a round shows and how many unique picks win the level.

recap.title: shuffleArray deals random, distinct cards
recap.body: Each round it draws distinct random positions from the pool until the board is full.

recap.title: verifyArray guards every deal
recap.body: A deal with no unpicked card is redrawn, so there is always a safe card to click.

recap.title: Card is face up, CardBack is face down
recap.body: Card draws the character's image; CardBack fills each slot while the board flips.

steps.title: Each level sets the board size
steps.why: levelSettings gives how many cards a round shows and how many unique picks win the level.

steps.title: shuffleArray picks this round's cards
steps.why: It draws distinct random positions from the pool until the round is full, then stores the dealt cards.

snippet.t: // loading, or the fetch failed) never spins this loop forever.

steps.title: A deal with nothing new is redrawn
steps.why: If the full deal holds no unpicked card, it starts over, so there is always a safe card to click.

steps.title: verifyArray is the unpicked-card guard
steps.why: It returns true as soon as one dealt position is still in the unpicked list.

steps.title: randomIntFromInterval rolls one position
steps.why: A whole number between min and max, both included. shuffleArray calls it once per card slot.

steps.title: Card shows a dealt character
steps.why: A face-up card draws the character's image from the API data.

steps.title: CardBack covers the board between deals
steps.why: While the board flips, PlayPage draws a face-down card in each slot.

recap.title: A run is saved once, under a typed name
recap.body: The end-game popup saves only when a name was typed and this run hasn't been saved yet.

recap.title: Runs are stored sorted, highest score first
recap.body: sortHighScores ranks the list, which is written as JSON to localStorage under highScoresKey.

recap.title: A missing or broken list loads as empty
recap.body: loadHighScores falls back to an empty list when the stored value is missing or corrupt.

recap.title: The trophy modal ranks runs per level
recap.body: HighScoresModal reloads saved runs on open and shows one tab per level.

steps.title: Saving needs a name, once per run
steps.why: The end-game popup saves only when a name was typed and this run hasn't been saved yet.

steps.title: sortHighScores ranks runs
steps.why: It returns a new list with the highest score first, leaving the original untouched.

steps.title: The list is written to localStorage
steps.why: The new run joins the sorted list, which is stored as JSON under highScoresKey.

snippet.t: let newEntry = {name: name, score: activeScore, level: isLevel};

steps.title: loadHighScores reads it back
steps.why: It parses the stored list and falls back to an empty list when it is missing or corrupt.

steps.title: entryLevel works out a run's level
steps.why: It uses the saved level, or infers one only when the score rules the others out, else null.

steps.title: levelLabel names the badge
steps.why: It turns a run into a label like Hard, or an empty string when the level can't be known.

steps.title: The trophy modal shows one tab per level
steps.why: It reloads saved runs on open and lists only the runs of the selected level's tab.

tours.title: How music and sound effects play

recap.title: Each page has its own looping music track
recap.body: The title screen and the game each keep one looping Audio in a ref, played while music is on.

recap.title: Volume goes through a gain node
recap.body: iOS ignores an Audio element's volume, so each track runs through a gain node instead.

recap.title: The volume setting survives a reload
recap.body: Moving the slider saves the volume as matchingGame_volume for the next visit.

recap.title: Button and card sounds are synthesized
recap.body: playSfx builds each tap, hit and miss from one oscillator; no audio files ship for them.

steps.title: HandleHomeAudio plays the title track
steps.why: It keeps one looping Audio for the home song in a ref and plays it while the music is on.

steps.title: HandlePlayAudio plays the game track
steps.why: The same pattern with the Namek theme, used on the play page.

steps.title: routeThroughGain sets volume with a gain node
steps.why: iOS ignores an Audio element's volume, so each track runs through a gain node whose gain follows the slider.

snippet.t: // so the context isn't born suspended by the autoplay policy.

steps.title: The volume is remembered
steps.why: Moving the slider updates the volume and saves it as matchingGame_volume for the next visit.

steps.title: One shared AudioContext
steps.why: Made on first use and reused by both the music gain and the sound effects.

steps.title: playSfx synthesizes a short sound
steps.why: Taps, hits and misses are one oscillator each, silent while the music toggle is off.
